title: POC Weekly: Onboarding & Staging Readiness - MavenPay
next_steps: Redwood to share updated bench spreadsheet with quant profiles
Customer to confirm SSO metadata and test SAML in staging
action_items: Ethan Brooks (Redwood) - run second round of 1k-query bench with batch=8 and share results by 2027-07-12
Rajiv Kapoor (MavenPay) - provide SAML IdP metadata and open firewall port for staging by 2027-07-09
Lena Cho (Redwood CSM) - upload onboarding checklist + access matrix to shared drive by 2027-07-08
meeting_header: Date: 2027-07-07 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood CSM), Rajiv Kapoor (MavenPay Platform Eng), Naomi Li (MavenPay SecOps), Ben Torres (MavenPay ML Infra)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on onboarding progress, credentialing for the staging environment, and interpretation of initial benchmark results. Discussed SSO/SAML handoff, KMS integration constraints, brief cost/latency tradeoffs when choosing Dedicated vs hosted, and scheduling deeper benchmark. Agreement to run another targeted latency/batch profile and complete credential handovers this week.
topics: Access matrix and RBAC for pilot teams
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we got 48 minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
[00:12] Rajiv - MavenPay: Rajiv here, Naomi and Ben on my side as well.
[00:18] Naomi - MavenPay: hi, thanks.
[00:22] Ethan (Redwood SE): Ethan here, bringing the bench notes. sorry for audio—my mic's a little tinny.
[00:28] Lena (Redwood CSM): Lena here, I will own the onboarding checklist follow-ups.
[00:35] Sofia (Redwood): sweet, agenda is: access and staging readiness, quick pass on the numbers from last week's bench, and KMS/SSO stuff. any other items?
[00:46] Rajiv - MavenPay: maybe also we want to talk about RBAC, who gets what in staging.
[00:52] Sofia (Redwood): yes we'll cover roles. ok Ethan, can you lead on the bench summary?
[01:05] Ethan (Redwood SE): yeah quick recap. last week we ran the sample 500-qps surrogate with quant-lite profile -- results: p50 token latency about 120ms, p95 around 320ms with batch size 4. we saw tail spikes when sequence lengths hit 1k. note: those were on hosted infra in the eu-west region — not yet on your dedicated staging pool.
[01:32] Ben Torres - MavenPay: small question, when you say quant-lite, is that int8 or mixed?
[01:38] Ethan (Redwood SE): mixed — it's our 8/16 hybrid we call q-lite, less aggressive than full int8. we can push a stricter q profile if you want more throughput at cost of occasional quality drift.
[01:48] Naomi - MavenPay: quality drift is a concern for compliance, we need to keep outputs stable for financial statements. also SOC 2 needs auditability—do you have logs?
[01:58] Sofia (Redwood): yep Redwood Console exposes token-level traces and per-request audit ids, plus optional retention policies we can tune. for SOC2 we have an SOC2+ pack, but of course for production you'd probably want our Private deployment or Dedicated depending on your residency needs.
[02:18] Rajiv - MavenPay: can Private run in our VPC? we have strict egress policies.
[02:24] Ethan (Redwood SE): yes Private supports VPC peering and air-gapped installs. but for the pilot we recommended Dedicated since it's faster to provision; Dedicated gives you reserved pools and is easier to measure throughput. Private has extra ops lead time.
[02:39] Rajiv - MavenPay: got it. timeline question — how long to flip Dedicated into our staging?
[02:45] Sofia (Redwood): once creds and firewall rules are set, typical turn-up is 3-5 business days. we're blocked right now by the SAML metadata and your KMS access pattern.
[02:56] Naomi - MavenPay: on KMS, we want to bring our key via CloudKMS but with restricted decrypt perms. can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[03:05] Ethan (Redwood SE): yes, we support bring-your-own KMS/HSM and can map service roles to limited decrypt-only keys. small caveat, if you want on-prem HSM we'll need a handshake for the HSM agent during install.
[03:21] Ben Torres - MavenPay: ok noted. next on the bench: any anomalies?
[03:25] Ethan (Redwood SE): one anomaly — KV cache hit ratio was lower than expected for the session pattern you shared. looks like prompt prefixes were varying more than we saw in dev data, so caching didn't help as much. we suggested canonicalization or a small prompt-normalization layer to improve hit-rate.
[03:44] Rajiv - MavenPay: yeah our prompts include dynamic headers per request. we can probably add a prefix template to increase cache reuse.
[03:50] Sofia (Redwood): that's a cheap win, we can share a snippet. we'll also include recommended batching windows.
[03:58] [04:00] Ethan (Redwood SE): ok moving on, I want to propose a targeted benchmark run: 1k queries at three batch sizes (2,4,8) with q-lite and full-int8. that should give a clearer throughput/latency curve for your traffic.
[04:14] Rajiv - MavenPay: sounds good. do you need anything from our side?
[04:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): SAML metadata to login the staging console and an IP range for the bench runner so we don't get blocked by your firewall. also a sample traffic trace (anonymized) would help.
[04:30] Naomi - MavenPay: we'll send the metadata today. firewall rules need to open 10.11.32.0/24 to your bench egress — I will raise the ticket.
[04:41] Sofia (Redwood): thanks. on RBAC — we prepared an access matrix template in the shared drive: drive.redwood.com/mavenpay/onboard (link). roles recommended: dev, sec, ops, analytics.
[04:55] Rajiv - MavenPay: do you have SSO test endpoints?
[04:58] Ethan (Redwood SE): yes we have a test SAML binder. we'll give you the metadata endpoint — it's under the console settings. note: sometimes IdP attributes are mapped differently, so there might be a quick mapping step.
[05:12] [05:15] Naomi - MavenPay: mapping is usually NameID and an attribute for groups. we'll confirm names.
[05:20] Ben Torres - MavenPay: security question — where are logs stored? can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[05:25] Sofia (Redwood): yes logs can be exported via secure syslog or S3 export to a customer bucket. we also have an API for per-request traces. for Private, you can keep logs on-prem.
[05:37] Rajiv - MavenPay: ok good.
[05:39] [06:00] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick note on cost/latency tradeoff — if you lean into batch=8 and full int8 on Dedicated you'll see about 30-40% lower per-token compute cost but p95 latency will shift up ~80-120ms in our tests. so it's a throughput play.
[06:18] Rajiv - MavenPay: hmm for payment flows we prefer low tail latency — p95 under 350ms ideally.
[06:25] Ethan (Redwood SE): we can aim for a conservative profile: batch=4, q-lite gives you p95 ~320ms in our runs. then we can do a canary with int8 on non-critical routes.
[06:36] Sofia (Redwood): also feature flagging at the application level can allow graceful degradation to a smaller model if tails spike.
[06:45] Rajiv - MavenPay: useful, we'll plan that.
[06:48] [07:00] Naomi - MavenPay: compliance — do you maintain an audit trail for who changed model versions?
[07:05] Sofia (Redwood): yes Console records rollouts, who triggered the canary, and you can lock model rollouts behind RBAC. we also keep immutable audit logs (append-only) for enterprise tiers.
[07:17] Ben Torres - MavenPay: one more infra nuance — your hosted EU nodes are fine, but our staging needs to be in us-east. is that available for Dedicated?
[07:26] Ethan (Redwood SE): yep we have us-east Dedicated pools; provisioning might add 48 hours if it's a new capacity cluster.
[07:34] Rajiv - MavenPay: ok. about creds: Naomi will give SAML and I'll open the firewall. Ben will coordinate KMS.
[07:43] [08:00] Lena (Redwood CSM): I'll drop the onboarding checklist link in the follow-up and set up a short runbook for the SAML mapping steps.
[08:09] Sofia (Redwood): great. any blockers we need to escalate?
[08:13] Rajiv - MavenPay: only the internal change freeze next week — might shift our timing by a day or two.
[08:18] Sofia (Redwood): that's fine; we'll target bench on 7/12 but flexible.
[08:23] [09:00] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick question on data retention settings — MavenPay, you mentioned stricter retention in prod. for pilot we can set retention to 7 days, prod can be 90 or custom per regs.
[09:33] Naomi - MavenPay: yeah for pilot 7 days is fine. production will be 90 and log export to our S3 will be retained per policy.
[09:42] Sofia (Redwood): perfect. I'm going to read back the immediate next steps: Redwood runs targeted bench (Ethan) and shares spreadsheet; MavenPay shares SAML metadata and opens firewall (Naomi/Rajiv); Redwood uploads onboarding docs (Lena).
[09:58] Rajiv - MavenPay: agreed. oh and pricing question — if we scale to Dedicated and then convert to Private later, is there a migration cost?
[10:07] Sofia (Redwood): there is a migration advisory fee and some infra handoff hours for Private installs — roughly estimated in the enterprise packet. we'll send numbers in the follow-up.
[10:19] Ben Torres - MavenPay: can you also include an approximate SLA for p99 in Dedicated?
[10:24] Ethan (Redwood SE): Dedicated SLA is typically on availability and p95 latency tiers; p99 is harder to guarantee due to noisy neighbors but with reserved nodes we can set stricter SLOs — we'll include a proposed SLA table.
[10:39] [11:00] Naomi - MavenPay: one last thing — do you support customer tokenization or redaction for PII?
[11:06] Sofia (Redwood): yes we support both redaction at ingress and post-response tokenization pipelines. there's a guide we'll share.
[11:13] Rajiv - MavenPay: excellent.
[11:16] [12:00] Sofia (Redwood): ok if no more questions, let's recap owner and due dates.
[12:24] Lena (Redwood CSM): recap: Ethan to run bench by 7/12; Rajiv/Naomi to provide SAML and firewall by 7/9; Lena to upload docs by 7/8; Sofia to send pricing and SLA packet by 7/9.
[12:45] Rajiv - MavenPay: that works.
[12:49] Ben Torres - MavenPay: thanks all.
[12:52] Sofia (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the bench template. bye.
[13:00] meeting end
